newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soyoil ends up on short covering, meal lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soyoil ends up on short covering, meal lower.

text.p: CBOT soyoil futures closed higher on late shortcovering and fund buying, with Rosenthal Collins called the key player on the long side during the waning five minutes of trading, traders said.
"It originated in oil and spilled into beans," a trader said of the late shortcovering rally "floorwide."

Technicians cited the ability of December to convincingly hold above chart support throughout the session. The first support level for December was seen at 22.53 cents per lb which was the session low and was set early.

Cargill Inc and ADM Investor Services each bought 300 lots of January and U.S. exporters said supplies of soyoil at the U.S. Gulf were tight and dealers were scrambling to find enough soyoil to load a vessel set to sail on December 12.
Also soyoil exports during the lastest week were "satisfactory" along with soybeans but the data for other commodities was well below expectations. Exports were very bearish for soymeal.
Soyoil closed 0.23 to 0.42 cent higher, with December up 0.42 at 23.05 cents a lb. Soymeal settled $0.50 lower to $2.00 higher, with December down $0.50 at $234.60 a ton.
USDA said U.S. net export sales of soyoil during the week totaled 15,400 tonnes, about mid-range of trade expectations from 10,000 to 20,000 tonnes.
Bearish input from USDA's weekly export sales report pressured nearby CBOT soymeal futures lower, the traders said.
"Not only were exports low but meal was a minus which was surprising," a trader said.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of soymeal during the week ended November 28 were at a minus 11,200 tonnes. The market was expecting a soymeal tally from 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes.
USDA cited cancellations of soymeal during the week from unknown destinations, China and the Netherlands.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, below the 24,589 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 32,000 contracts, above the 25,056 traded Wednesday.
